The story

0xDOGE launched on February 16, 2018, just 10 days after 0xBitcoin. 0xBitcoin was a coin on Ethereum that people earned by having their computers solve math puzzles, the same way Bitcoin works. 0xDOGE was the first copy of it.

Its code had two mistakes: one in how rewards were calculated, and one in a built-in limit that tripped over itself. Together they made 0xDOGE stop working forever after only 12 payouts. Nobody can earn new coins from it, and nobody ever will.

That left exactly 1.2 million coins in existence, with no way to make more. 0xDOGE was the first coin of its kind on Ethereum to permanently break itself.
